title: Blankets
author: Craig Thompson
current_text: In September 2006, Marshall, Missouri resident Louise Mills challenged Blankets at the Marshall Public Library, seeking its removal over illustrations she alleged were obscene and likened to pornography; the challenge was referred to the Library Board of Trustees. In March 2007, the Marshall Public Library Board approved a materials selection policy that was immediately applied to Blankets, restoring it to the library collection.

sources.quote: Louise Mills, a resident of Marshall, MO, filed a request with the Marshall Public Library Board of Trustees to have Blankets removed from the shelves because of the allegedly obscene illustrations. She likened the illustrations to pornography and was concerned that the comic art would attract children who would subsequently see the images she alleged were pornographic.
sources.title: Case Study: Blankets – Comic Book Legal Defense Fund

sources.quote: In September 2006, two graphic novels [Fun Home by Alison Bechdel and Blankets by Craig Thompson] were challenged by a resident of Marshall, Missouri. In accordance with library policy at that time, any challenges were referred to the Library Board of Trustees
sources.title: 10 Years After a Challenge - Amy Crump - Intellectual Freedom Blog

sources.quote: The Materials Selection Policy [current policy starts on pg. 34] for the Marshall Public Library was approved by the Board in March 2007 and immediately applied to the challenged materials, resulting in the books being restored to the library collection.
sources.title: 10 Years After a Challenge - Amy Crump - Intellectual Freedom Blog
